Tympany there reflects trapped gas proximal to a fecal mass. The absence of tenderness, peritoneal signs, or systemic toxicity further supports a benign, functional GI etiology over surgical or septic pathology.  

Base-rate prior strongly favors functional constipation: it is extremely common in infants starting solids (~10–25% prevalence), often underdiagnosed due to subtle or atypical presentations (e.g., decreased intake, irritability, rather than overt constipation), and fully consistent with all documented findings. No finding contradicts it; all supportive findings align. More serious diagnoses require *additional* features (e.g., bilious vomiting for obstruction; fever + pyuria for UTI; leukocytosis or bandemia for SBI) — none present.
